notes.security_ocspd: CONFIRMED DISABLED. server/main.cpp:104-112 logs that ocspd is disabled (subsumed by trustd since macOS 12) and exit(1) before any run loop. LaunchDaemon plist still present; binary aborts on invoke. Network fetch / CRL paths unreachable.
notes.configd: Reviewed session.c checkWriteAccess/hasRootAccess/entitlements, SCDPlugin fork/execv with fixed paths, IPMonitor system() only in TEST_* builds. No unauthenticated SCDynamicStore write bypass validated.
notes.SMBClient: Reviewed parse_url, mount paths, kernel smb_crypt decompress (cap originalCompressedSegmentSize <= kDefaultMaxIOSize 8MiB; compress_len vs remaining_size). No complete remote kernel or local priv-esc chain validated.
notes.syslog: aslmanager XPC accept_connection only runs main_task when peer euid == geteuid. udp_in is unauthenticated log intake when socket configured — no command sink from message body.
notes.NFS: com.apple.nfsd.plist KeepAlive PathState /etc/exports — not active by default. mountd host matching via find_host/OP_DEFEXP; check_dirpath rejects symlink components. No stock unauthenticated export without admin enabling NFS.
notes.autofs: automountd MIG requires audit_token pid==0 (kernel). fstype concatenated into /sbin/mount_%s without '/' filter, but map sources are /etc and OD (admin); mount helpers run as sendereuid via posix_spawnattr_set_uid_np. No unprivileged complete chain.
notes.kext_tools: Non-root load limited to Extensions/System Filesystems with realpath revalidation; OSKextIsAuthentic/staging COPYFILE_NOFOLLOW. No unprivileged unsigned load chain.
notes.file_cmds: No setuid install modes; userland tools only. No privileged attack surface for local escalation alone.
notes.security_certificates: Static roots/pinning assets and CertificateTool build helpers; no runtime privileged daemon in this tree.

prior_pass_findings_preserved.title: Use-after-free in mod_hfs_apple non-ASCII path comparison
prior_pass_findings_preserved.description: compare_non_ascii_paths() CFRelease()s parentRef and childRef, then immediately passes those freed CFStringRefs into CFStringCreateWithSubstring(). Directory entries and request paths are always normalized with a trailing slash, so both UAF branches execute for every non-ASCII URI that reaches the fixup hook. mod_hfs_apple is LoadModule'd in Apple's httpd.conf patch and listed among httpd-wrapper default active modules.
prior_pass_findings_preserved.impact: Unauthenticated remote HTTP requests can corrupt heap memory in the Apache worker (typically _www). Reliable process crash (DoS); with heap grooming, potential remote code execution in the httpd process.
prior_pass_findings_preserved.attack_path: 1) Enable/run Apple httpd with mod_hfs_apple (default when Web Sharing/Server httpd is on). 2) Ensure at least one <Directory> applies (default DocumentRoot). 3) Send HTTP request whose mapped filename contains a non-ASCII UTF-8 byte (e.g. /café/ or percent-encoded multi-byte UTF-8). 4) fixups -> compare_paths -> compare_non_ascii_paths: CFRelease then CFStringCreateWithSubstring on freed refs. 5) Crash or exploit UAF for code execution as the httpd user.
prior_pass_findings_preserved.remediation: Strip the trailing slash before release: create the substring from the live CFStringRef first, then CFRelease the original. Example: tmp = CFStringCreateWithSubstring(NULL, parentRef, range); CFRelease(parentRef); parentRef = tmp; Same for childRef. Add regression tests with non-ASCII URIs and AddressSanitizer.
prior_pass_findings_preserved.why_exploitable: Network-reachable without authentication whenever httpd+mod_hfs_apple serves content. Trigger condition (non-ASCII path + trailing slash) is guaranteed by the module's own path normalization. CFRelease-then-use is classic undefined behavior that modern allocators make exploitable.

prior_pass_findings_preserved.title: WebDAV redirect accepts attacker Location/X-Apple-MMe-Host enabling SSRF and mount-credential replay
prior_pass_findings_preserved.description: nodecache_redirect_node() builds the new base URL from the server's Location header (or X-Apple-MMe-Host for status 330) with no host allowlist. The only check blocks https→http downgrade. After root redirect, gBaseURL is replaced. On subsequent 401s, AddServerCredentials() prefers CopyMountCredentials() and can send the original mount username/password to the redirected host.
prior_pass_findings_preserved.impact: A malicious WebDAV server can pivot the mounted filesystem agent to arbitrary http(s) URLs (SSRF from the client host as the mounting user) and obtain the mount credentials when the redirect target challenges for auth.
prior_pass_findings_preserved.attack_path: 1) Victim mounts https://evil.example/share with username/password. 2) evil.example responds 302/330 with Location or X-Apple-MMe-Host pointing at https://attacker-collector/ or an internal https service. 3) nodecache_redirect_node updates gBaseURL/redir_name. 4) Later requests go to the attacker-chosen host; on 401, authcache CreateAuthenticationFromResponse → AddServerCredentials → CopyMountCredentials sends mount credentials to that host.
prior_pass_findings_preserved.remediation: Restrict redirects to the original host (or an explicit allowlist). Never change gBaseURL to a different host without user confirmation. Do not replay mount credentials to a host different from the one used at mount time; clear kCredentialsFromMount / force re-prompt on cross-host redirects.
prior_pass_findings_preserved.why_exploitable: Mounting a remote WebDAV share is a normal user action. The server fully controls Location/X-Apple-MMe-Host. Cross-host redirect plus mount-credential-first authcache behavior yields both SSRF and credential theft without further bugs.
